title: The River Lantern City
premise: A dense river city survives seasonal floods through guild-managed medicine, waterways, and public memory rituals; private choices are constrained by obligations that remain visible in everyday space.
scope: One city, its upstream farming basin, and the social systems needed for a short dramatic film.

canon.statement: The lower wards flood predictably each late summer.
canon.rationale: This pressure shapes architecture, transport, labor, and the story deadline.

canon.statement: Households float one marked lantern for each publicly acknowledged debt.
canon.rationale: The ritual externalizes reputation but still requires user approval.

canon.statement: No treatment cures severe illness instantly or without trade-offs.
canon.rationale: Medical choices must retain dramatic cost.

systems.name: Guild medicine
rules: Licensed houses share flood-season triage duties.
Patient records create social obligations as well as clinical history.
limits: Knowledge and supplies vary by district.
costs: Breaking guild duty risks license, household income, and public trust.
exceptions: Emergency aid may be given before identity is recorded.

geography.name: Lower Ward
geography.scale: A walkable canal district of six linked blocks.
geography.orientation: The medical guild hall sits uphill north; the ferry steps and courtyard houses descend south toward the river.
relationships: Three narrow bridges connect the lower ward to the market spine.
Floodwater first enters through the southern ferry lane.

societies.name: Medical guild households
powerStructure: Senior license holders allocate supplies and apprenticeships.
everydayLife: Consultations open before the market and continue after dusk during flood season.
conflicts: Household loyalty can oppose equal treatment across districts.

history.name: The Great Flood generation
events: A failed embankment erased the old southern ward.
lastingConsequences: Guild duty is enforced through public debt records.

history.name: Present flood season
events: Repairs are incomplete as the next heavy rains arrive.
lastingConsequences: Private reconciliation competes with urgent civic duty.

possible: Characters can cross districts by foot, skiff, or bridge.
impossible: A character cannot erase a public debt without witnesses noticing.
costly: Defying guild orders risks both livelihood and patient access.
storyHooks: Two former intimates meet while triaging a flood-threatened household.

wardrobeLogic: layered practical clothing communicates trade, duty, and wet-weather adaptation
physicalLightLogic: oil flame and reflected water motivate night light

immutableFacts: north-south slope from guild hall to river
continuityPolicy.conflictResolution: Surface same-namespace conflicts for human decision; never select the newest statement automatically.

unknowns: Exact historical analogues remain intentionally unspecified.

locks.reason: Scene geography and screen direction depend on the uphill-north relationship.
The world defines physical design, while Style owns representation.
